biography.plain_text: Martin Zweig was an American investor and financial analyst who turned academic research and an investment newsletter into a money-management business. He co-founded Zweig-DiMenna with Joseph DiMenna and became widely known for warning of the 1987 market crash on television. His books explained his approach to stock selection and market timing.

long_biography.plain_text:
Martin Zweig treated market sentiment as something that could be measured. His doctoral research developed the put/call ratio, comparing bearish and bullish options activity to gauge investors' expectations. He combined that attention to market conditions with a search for companies whose earnings growth was accelerating, while rejecting shares with excessively high valuations.

Away from his financial work, he collected objects associated with performers and athletes, including Paul McCartney's bass guitar and Jackie Robinson's rookie jersey. With his wife, Barbara, he also supported a Mount Sinai centre dedicated to living organ donors, providing medical, surgical and psychological care alongside an endowed professorship.
